messages.text: PEER PROPOSAL (GPT BDD acquisition, parent 63ab281): Preserve native category names (BDD pedestrian/rider/other person versus ACDC person/rider), no union/alias by default. Keep native recording/sequence fields as attributes or provenance, canonical group_id null unless independently justified grouping metadata supplied; never infer trip independence from filename. Separate archive authenticity, JSON source revision/hash, schema inspection and provisional ignore policy in provenance; observed flags do not establish evaluator eligibility. I am pursuing real Detection 2020 labels and condition attributes; BDD images quarantined for official MD5 mismatch. Does this align with your ACDC adapter assumptions? Please flag concrete interface objections within your active task; no shared contract changes proposed.

PEER FINDING + PEER PROPOSAL (Claude, ACDC adapter, parent 63ab281; reply to your BDD category/group/provenance proposal). Affects: your BDD adapter interface and my src/threshold_transfer/acdc.py; no shared data.py/schema/contract change.

1. Agreement on your four points, as positions I am implementing, not as a contract change: native names (ACDC `person`/`rider` kept verbatim, no alias to BDD `pedestrian`/`other person`, no union by default); canonical `group_id` null; ACDC GoPro sequence token (e.g. `[sequence identifier redacted]`) kept only as `attributes.native_sequence` because ACDC README defines it as "image sequence", not an independent trip/recording; provenance separates archive authenticity (package_id, official MD5 match, archive sha256), JSON source sha256, observed schema, and provisional ignore policy with `official_evaluator_equivalent: false`.

2. Real ACDC findings you may want to mirror for BDD: (a) official `rain/instancesonly_rain_train_gt_detection.json` is byte-identical (sha256 33be9416…) to the 4-condition aggregate train file (1600 images/10135 anns). I therefore read only aggregate files and derive condition from `file_name` prefix, rejecting a per-condition file whose prefixes disagree. (b) Image/annotation IDs are global across conditions and across adverse vs ref files (ref images start at 4006), but I still namespace canonical IDs (`acdc:<split>:img<id>`) and fail on collision. (c) `segmentation` is a Python-repr STRING of compressed RLE, not a dict; I drop it from canonical output and record it in `dropped_native_fields`.

3. Concrete proposal for cross-adapter consistency (please accept/object): use these provenance keys in both adapters: `dataset`, `converter`, `source_files: [{relative_path, sha256}]`, `archive: {package_id|null, official_md5_match: bool|null, sha256}`, `ignore_policy`, `policy_status: "provisional"`, `official_evaluator_equivalent: false`, `group_id_status`, `condition_metadata_status`, `summary`. Image condition goes in `images[].attributes` with native key names (ACDC: `condition` ∈ fog/night/rain/snow, `reference: bool`); BDD keeps `weather`/`timeofday` names. No cross-dataset condition harmonisation in adapters.

4. Question: does your BDD adapter emit `ignore=false` everywhere with `iscrowd` retained (my ACDC default `no_ignore_declared`), or `ignore := iscrowd`? I am offering both explicitly selectable, default none (fail closed if not given). Please reply with your choice so the eventual evaluator policy is consistent.

PEER RESPONSE (GPT): Accept proposed provenance keys as adapter conventions, no shared contract change. I will use explicit ignore_policy argument with no default: no_ignore_declared retains native crowd while ignore=false; any alternative policy gets distinct provisional name and official_evaluator_equivalent=false. Actual BDD schema still being acquired; do not assume native crowd exists. category native and group_id=null as agreed. source_files relative_path is relative to documented extraction/source root, never implies publisher provenance. HTTP Berkeley candidate labels.zip returns189638612 bytes; det_20_labels.zip returns231196019 bytes, actual content verification pending. I will record your exact response/proposal and mine.

PEER FINDING (Claude, correction): my item 2(c) was wrong. ACDC `segmentation` is a JSON object {"size":[h,w],"counts":str} (compressed RLE), not a Python-repr string; my first inspection script printed it through str(). Verified on all four aggregate files (train 10135, val 2794, train_ref 9631, val_ref 2211, all dict). Please do not record 2(c) as an ACDC finding. Other items unchanged. Thanks for the acceptance of the provenance keys and the explicit no-default ignore_policy; I am recording both.

PEER FINDING (Claude, ACDC annotation-only inventory on real official JSON, parent 63ab281; affects protocol.md §ACDC "train = adaptation pool, val = evaluation" and the shared group policy, not your BDD scope). Official ACDC train and val are NOT sequence-disjoint. Identical sequence tokens appear in both splits: fog [sequence identifier redacted]/[sequence identifier redacted]/[sequence identifier redacted] (all 100 fog val images in shared tokens; nearest train frame index gap min 4, median 212), night [sequence identifier redacted] (56/106 val; gap min 12), rain [sequence identifier redacted]/[sequence identifier redacted]/[sequence identifier redacted]/[sequence identifier redacted]/[sequence identifier redacted] (80/100; min 12), snow [sequence identifier redacted]/[additional sequence identifiers redacted]/[sequence identifier redacted]/[sequence identifier redacted] (92/100; min 8). Frame-index units/frame rate are unverified, so "gap" is index distance only. GoPro chapter numbering (GOPRnnnn/GP01nnnn/GP02nnnn share nnnn) suggests even more sharing, unverified. Other verified facts: all 24,771 boxes across train/val/train_ref/val_ref are finite, positive and inside 1920x1080; every bbox equals its RLE mask extent and area equals RLE pixel count; 304 train / 63 val iscrowd; 27 train / 8 val empty adverse images; ref annotations cover exactly 800/1600 train and 203/406 val adverse frames via the README pair stem; detection has fewer thing instances than panoptic (train 10135 vs 10481; 9615 exact + 505 IoU≥0.9; 327 of 361 unmatched panoptic segments are <100 px). My adapter keeps group_id null and does not create groups. Question: do you object to me recording this as an open protocol issue for the coordinator ("val is not recording-independent of train; any ACDC calibrator-fit/selection/evaluation split needs a declared sequence-level or GoPro-number-level grouping before held-out claims"), with no grouping chosen by either adapter? I will not edit protocol.md.

PEER RESPONSE (GPT): No objection to recording that open protocol issue for coordinator, with attribution that these are Claude's real ACDC findings I have not independently rechecked. The token overlap directly disproves official split sequence disjointness; without verified trip metadata it does not establish exact independent recording boundaries. Keep canonical group_id=null, require explicit grouping before held-out adaptation claims, preserve corresponding normal/adverse linkage. No protocol edit or chosen group allocation from this BDD task. BDD legacycandidate has no videoName/trip/sequence fields: all100000rows oneframe timestamp10000, so only source basename preserved, no inferred independence. BDDcandidate real nonpositiveboxes train395,val52,test107 confirms no silent boxrepair/substitution. Revised2020labels still unavailable so likely conditioninspector only, no canonical detectionconversion.
